audits.text:
## 73ab3e5ab7dc

**Reproduced domain restriction / shortcut gap.** The authoritative rule is global color frequency, but selected generator SHA-256 `687ace5fafa7e45f4b1d46d8da5f030c4429109c8c5b83ac12f19a165dff51fc` requires each nonzero color to form exactly one 4-connected component. That restriction is not part of the Racket rule, and two canonical pairs already contain a split majority color.

I constructed a lawful two-color, unequal-frequency input in which color 2 has four cells split into two 2-cell components while color 3 has one connected 3-cell component. Canonical Racket rule `7abba8faba35` chooses color 2 by global count and recolors all seven cells to 2. The plausible rival `largest_single_component_wins` chooses color 3 instead. The outputs disagree, while the selected `self_check` rejects the input solely because color 2 has two components. This means generated lessons cannot distinguish the intended global-frequency rule from the largest-component shortcut on this axis.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/73ab3e5ab7dc/split-majority-input.json`
- `checks/audit/73ab3e5ab7dc/racket-apply.json` — supported canonical Racket execution, source/rule/input/output hashes, and validator-domain result.
- `checks/audit/73ab3e5ab7dc/largest-component-rival-counterexample.json` — exact rival output, per-color global/component counts, and the two canonical split-color examples.
- Command from packet root: `python3 review.py run python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 73ab3e5ab7dc --input ../checks/audit/73ab3e5ab7dc/split-majority-input.json --check-generator-domain --out ../checks/audit/73ab3e5ab7dc/racket-apply.json` (exit 0).

**Disposition:** finding only. I did not edit this audit target. Recommended repair is to permit multiple same-color components and add generated witnesses where global frequency and largest-component size select opposite colors.
